rows.headline: US Labor Department expands J-1 visa fraud probes to more universities
rows.hook: US visa crackdown targets top research universities
rows.summary: US Department of Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito announced that additional US universities will face investigations for potential J-1 visa fraud, following probes launched into nine institutions including Harvard, Yale, and MIT. Vice President JD Vance alleged that these universities used the exchange visitor programme to bring in foreign researchers at lower wages than American workers. The newly formed Visa Fraud Strike Team will also investigate high-risk programmes like H-1B visas. Indian students and researchers planning to pursue academic or research positions in the US face heightened scrutiny amid these federal probes.
rows.why_it_matters: Higher hurdles for US academic and research visas.
